name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+40 partisan lean makes a Democratic hold overwhelming
Chris Rabb won the Democratic primary and has strong fundraising plus outside support
Independent Dennis Mahoney is minimally funded with no outside backing
Open seat removes incumbency but not the district's structural advantage
model.rationale: The D+40 fundamentals make this seat effectively unwinnable for the opposition, and Rabb's financial edge over an underfunded independent reinforces that. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays at Safe D.
model.watch: A surprise surge in independent Mahoney's fundraising or name recognition would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Philadelphia's PA-03 is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+40. Dwight Evans is retiring, leaving an open seat, but the Democratic nominee Chris Rabb enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised over $1.3 million and drawn substantial outside support. His opponent, independent Dennis Mahoney, has raised only about $10,800 with no outside spending on his behalf.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97 percent, consistent with the district's fundamentals. With no public polls and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on the seat's structural lean and the lopsided resource gap, both pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold.
